data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 argues that decentralized networks are more resilient specifically because they use lazy/eventual consistency while large services use strict consistency. This conflates an architectural choice (consistency model) with the degree of centralization, so the argument fails the problem's comparison as stated. The problem asks about a 'decentralized network of small, independently operated services' versus 'one large service with strictly more total internal redundancy' — it does not stipulate their consistency protocols. A large service can be built on an eventual-consistency or partition-tolerant design (e.g., a globally replicated AP datastore with massive internal redundancy), and a decentralized network can require synchronous consensus (SRC_001 even concedes this in a countercondition). Under such a configuration, SRC_001's claimed mechanism vanishes: the decentralized network halts on a failure while the large service partitions and continues. Because the causal argument rests on an incidental feature that is not implied by either side of the comparison, it cannot establish that decentralization itself yields greater resilience to correlated failure.
